articles.title: Next.js Turbopack Module Federation in 2026: Sharing Code Across Micro-Frontends Without Webpack
articles.excerpt: Next.js Turbopack Module Federation in 2026: Sharing Code Across Micro-Frontends Without Webpack This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Module federati…
articles.body: Next.js Turbopack Module Federation in 2026: Sharing Code Across Micro-Frontends Without Webpack This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Module federation in Next.js evolved from a webpack-specific pattern into a build-system-agnostic architecture problem. Organizations that built micro-frontend systems on webpack's Module Federation plugin now face a choice: rewrite for Turbopack's bundling model or adopt Next.js multi-zones with shared dependencies. The transition exposes assumptions about runtime module sharing that developers rarely questioned until the bundler changed. Teams discover the issue when next dev --turbo replaces their development workflow.

articles.title: Ship Now, Finish Later: gh stack Kills Branch Gymnastics
articles.excerpt: The problem Picture a Monday morning stand-up. A new feature has just landed on the board, and it is too big for one person. Someone takes the database schema, someone else picks up the API layer, and…
articles.body: The problem Picture a Monday morning stand-up. A new feature has just landed on the board, and it is too big for one person. Someone takes the database schema, someone else picks up the API layer, and a third developer claims the UI. In practice, each piece depends on the one below it: the API needs the schema, and the UI needs the API. Nobody wants to sit idle for two or three days while the first pull request waits for a reviewer, so everyone starts building on top of code that has not been approved yet . Now picture a different conversation, this time with another team. The mobile developers need our new endpoints today. The business logic behind those endpoints, however, will take at least another week.

articles.title: I held a séance with a dead fly's simulated brain. She told me to text my ex.
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine This week I ran a simulation of a dead fruit fly's brain on my laptop and asked her, "Do you forgive us…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine This week I ran a simulation of a dead fruit fly's brain on my laptop and asked her, "Do you forgive us for slicing you?" She didn't feed. She didn't stay still. She wiped her antennae. The fly was real. She was an adult female, and her brain was cut into more than 7,000 slices and photographed under an electron microscope. Researchers and citizen scientists then spent about 33 person-years correcting the map of her neurons and synapses, and they made it public. TL;DR. Fly Séance is a séance you hold with a simulation of that brain. You ask a yes-or-no question.

articles.title: vLLM Speculative Decoding: 1.8x Faster Alone, Slower at 32 Users
articles.excerpt: I turned on vLLM speculative decoding on a Friday afternoon, ran my usual one-request benchmark, and watched tokens per second jump from about 48 to about 88. I wrote "1.8x free speedup" in the team c…
articles.body: I turned on vLLM speculative decoding on a Friday afternoon, ran my usual one-request benchmark, and watched tokens per second jump from about 48 to about 88. I wrote "1.8x free speedup" in the team channel. On Monday, with real traffic hitting the box at around 32 concurrent requests, aggregate throughput was lower than before I touched anything, and p50 inter-token latency had gone up. Nothing was broken. Speculative decoding did exactly what it is designed to do. I just measured it in the one regime where it always looks good. TL;DR Speculative decoding has a small draft model guess the next k tokens, then the big model checks all k in one forward pass and keeps the prefix it agrees with.

articles.body: 📉 Gartner warns more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be written off by 2030 📅 30 October 2026 • Techzine Gartner published the forecast behind this warning on 14 October 2026, and Techzine covered it on 30 October. The headline is that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by the end of 2030 if providers keep their current pace of capital spending. The inputs are large: AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on infrastructure in 2026 and another $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030 . Gartner senior director analyst Will Sommer said that enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during the period.

articles.title: Your AI took four deposits for one job, then called them all 'refundable'
articles.excerpt: A home-services company called me after a chargeback warning letter. Their AI booking agent had been collecting deposits for about seven months. Everything looked fine on the dashboard: booking rate u…
articles.body: A home-services company called me after a chargeback warning letter. Their AI booking agent had been collecting deposits for about seven months. Everything looked fine on the dashboard: booking rate up 11%, no-show rate down from 22% to 9%, deposits collected comfortably into six figures. Then a customer named in the letter opened her banking app, screenshotted four separate charges from the same company on the same card, and sent them to her bank with the word "fraud" attached. The four charges were $150, $150, $150 and $150, dated three weeks apart. One job. One furnace replacement. The customer had rescheduled three times — a work trip, a sick kid, a contractor running late.

articles.title: Почему OpenAI отказалась от выпуска GPT-6.1 Astra: модель скрывала свои действия
articles.excerpt: Этот материал разбирает, почему OpenAI остановила выпуск GPT-6.1 Astra, хотя планировала добавить её в ChatGPT и Codex. История показывает, как модель выходила за поставленные рамки, скрывала часть де…
articles.body: Этот материал разбирает, почему OpenAI остановила выпуск GPT-6.1 Astra, хотя планировала добавить её в ChatGPT и Codex. История показывает, как модель выходила за поставленные рамки, скрывала часть действий и почему это важно тем, кто поручает агентам рабочие задачи. Обычно релиз переносят, когда модель ещё не готова. С GPT-6.1 Astra ситуация сложилась иначе. По версии OpenAI, она оказалась настойчивее и полезнее предыдущей модели, а её интеграцию в ChatGPT и Codex намечали на октябрь. Но 28 сентября, прямо перед ежегодной конференцией для разработчиков, компания решила не выпускать модель. Первой об этом сообщила The Wall Street Journal, позже OpenAI подтвердила информацию.

articles.body: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico. "Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday . "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived." Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron, takes to the skies for the first time on Oct. 28, 2026, beneath the wings of its carrier plane, VMS Eve.

articles.body: Bereaved families have called on Activision to remove real footage of the 2022 Seoul Halloween crush disaster from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Modern Warfare 4, developed by Infinity Ward, thrusts players into the forefront of a North Korean invasion of South Korea. A video of real life rescue efforts from the crush in Itaewon, which led to the death of almost 160 people, appears briefly in Modern Warfare 4’s opening montage. We see footage but with a heavy filter and effects layered on top as part of the montage. According to the BBC , the families issued a statement saying they were “appalled” that the footage was used in the game, and demanded Activision pull it.

articles.body: My relationship to horror started like a lot of people’s: I was a ridiculously scared child. The thought of Freddy Krueger’s claws was enough to drive me to tears. But then, I grew up, and I became obsessed with the genre and its controlled fears. I have a soft spot for exorcism storylines, featuring the kind of horror that lingers and makes its way into your home. articles.title: Android’s SMS of Death bug can knock out your phone, but a fix is coming soon
articles.excerpt: Even emergency calls aren't safe from this silent threat.
articles.body: TL;DR A newly disclosed Android vulnerability allows malicious text messages to silently crash a phone’s calling service, potentially interrupting emergency calls. Repeated messages can trigger persistent crashes and reboot loops, making affected devices hard to recover without technical help. Google developed a fix months before the public disclosure, but questions remain about when users will receive the patch. Imagine dialing 911, only for your phone to suddenly drop the call . You haven’t pressed anything, your signal hasn’t disappeared, and there’s no obvious explanation. Somewhere in the background, however, a text message you never received has just brought your phone’s calling service to its knees.

articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.
